newsitem.title: UK: BT cleans up its act over competitors - Oftel.
newsitem.headline: BT cleans up its act over competitors - Oftel.

text.p: Don Cruickshank, head of UK telecoms regulator Oftel, said that he had no present plans for further action against British Telecom over earlier instances of giving misleading information about competitors.

Cruickshank issued a provisional order against BT in September, requiring it to put in place measures necessary to prevent staff from engaging in such anti-competitive behaviour. Such an order lapses if it is not confirmed within three months.
Cruickshank said that BT was getting its house in order.
"...BT's response has demonstrated real commitment to the challenge of fair trading," Cruickshank said.

"It has produced and implemented a compliance plan which ought progressively to eliminate the sorts of behaviour towards other operators which was encountered by the Consumers' Association," he added.

Cruickshank said he would not hesitate to issue further orders should the problem resurface. "But even that is no substitute for BT eliminating the problem at root: it now has the means to do so and they must be let to work."
